newsitem.title: USA: Transco gas line open despite NY bomb scare.
newsitem.headline: Transco gas line open despite NY bomb scare.

text.p: A bomb scare forcing the precautionary closure of Buckeye Pipeline Co's fuel line on Staten Island, N.Y., so far has had no impact on Transco's nearby natural gas line, the company said Wednesday.
"We don't anticipate any disruption in service," said Chris Stockton, a spokesman for Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco), a subsidiary of Williams Cos Inc.
"But we're sending out two groups to inspect the area. Police are at the scene, the FBI are at the scene, and they are preparing to remove the device," he said.

Transco's 26-inch diameter lateral line runs parallel to the Buckeye petroleum products line, which carries jet fuel to John F. Kennedy International airport in the New York City borough of Queens, northeast of Staten Island across the entrance to New York Harbor.
The Transco line feeds into Brooklyn Union's local natural gas delivery network.
Buckeye Pipeline, owned by Buckeye Partners LP, said earlier Wednesday it had shut its line after police on Staten Island found a suspicious package near a section of its line.
